blocks.content: Ethan Carter had memorized this street the way other people memorized their own handwriting. Not intentionally. Just through repetition.
Six-thirty run. Eight o'clock coffee. Corner table, two sugars. Same every day.
He told himself this was efficient. Other people called it predictable. He'd stopped correcting them.

He turned past Bellamy Street, slowing where the road sloped toward the older part of town. The cracked green door on the bookstore. The bakery venting warm air onto the sidewalk like a bribe. The orange cat in the antique shop window that had never once acknowledged him.
He filed things like that. What happened when you didn't talk much — you ended up with a very detailed catalog of everything else.
The Copper Mug glowed at the end of the block. He pressed one hand into the stitch forming at his side and slowed to a walk.
Freelance artist. Nineteen. Two sugars. That's the whole morning in one sentence. Sounds better than: I paint whatever people will pay for and hope it's enough to keep going.
The bus hissed to a stop at the curb.
Gray suit. Grocery bags. Kid with headphones. He'd timed this run enough times to narrate it from memory.
Then red hair.
She stepped off the bus like she'd made a decision about the morning and the morning had agreed. Paper cup, one shoulder bag, a silver bracelet catching the early light.
She laughed at something on her phone. Not politely. A real one — the kind that escaped before a person could stop it.
Ethan looked away too fast.
Don't be weird.
He crouched and pretended to retie a shoe that was not untied.

By the time he stood up, she was crossing toward the arcade two blocks down — the one with the flickering neon that still promised TOKENS — PRIZES — FUN like it had been waiting twenty years for the right person to take it seriously.
He watched half a second too long.
She's beautiful.
Easy thought. Unhelpful thought.
You once charged a man two hundred dollars to put his motorcycle in space. Calibrate accordingly.
He started running before the silence could agree with him.
